description: Cross-panel reasoning probes: questions that require information from BOTH panels to answer. Tests whether models can integrate visual information across sub-plots.

figures.panel_description: (a) chemistry domain word co-occurrences, (b) mathematics domain word co-occurrences for the word 'reaction'

questions.question: The word 'the' appears in both panels. In which domain does it have a higher co-occurrence percentage, and by how much?
questions.expected: 'the' is 31% in chemistry (a) and 38% in mathematics (b). Higher in math by 7 percentage points.
questions.requires: Reading same category across both panels and computing difference

questions.question: Panel (a) has 6 word categories while panel (b) has fewer. What words appear in (a) but NOT in (b)?
questions.expected: (a) has: the, this, for, chemical, to, in. (b) has: the, $, equilibrium, constant. Words in (a) not in (b): this, for, chemical, to, in.

questions.question: Which domain shows a more concentrated distribution — does chemistry or mathematics have a more dominant top word? Support your answer with numbers from both panels.
questions.expected: Mathematics is more concentrated — 'the' at 38% vs chemistry 'the' at 31%. Also math has only 4 categories vs chemistry's 6, meaning fewer words capture more of the distribution.
questions.requires: Comparing distribution shapes across panels with numerical evidence

figures.panel_description: Top: Easy Training Set rewards, Bottom: Hard Training Set rewards. Both show Llama-On-Policy vs LUFFY over 500 steps.

questions.question: At step 500, which method (Llama-On-Policy or LUFFY) has a larger performance gap between Easy and Hard training sets?
questions.expected: Need to read final values for both methods on both panels. LUFFY appears to have similar final values on both Easy and Hard (~0.35-0.4), while Llama-On-Policy may differ more between Easy (~0.3) and Hard (~0.25). So Llama-On-Policy likely has the larger gap.
questions.requires: Reading 4 values (2 methods × 2 panels) and comparing cross-panel differences

questions.question: Does LUFFY converge faster on the Easy set or the Hard set? At approximately what step does each reach its plateau?
questions.expected: Compare the convergence point of the red LUFFY line in both panels. On Easy it may plateau around step 100-150, on Hard around step 150-200.
questions.requires: Identifying convergence points in both panels and comparing

questions.question: If you could only train on one dataset (Easy or Hard), which would you choose based on LUFFY's final reward, and does the choice differ for Llama-On-Policy?
questions.expected: Requires reading final rewards for both methods on both panels and making a judgment. This tests reasoning about which training regime is better for each method.
questions.requires: Cross-panel value comparison + reasoning about training implications

figures.panel_description: (a) 3B models on MATH-500, (b) 1.5B models on MATH-500, (c) 67B models on MATH-500, (d-f) same groups on AIME24

questions.question: Compare the best-performing model in panel (a) with the best in panel (c). How much does scaling from 3B to 67B improve the top score on MATH-500?
questions.expected: Panel (a) best is ~78.2%, panel (c) best is ~97.3%. Improvement of about 19 percentage points.
questions.requires: Reading max values from two different panels and computing difference

questions.question: Is the ranking of methods (CoT vs TTS) consistent between MATH-500 panels (a-c) and AIME24 panels (d-f)?
questions.expected: Need to check if the same method wins across both benchmark sets. Rankings may shift between benchmarks.

questions.question: Looking at panels (d) and (e), which model size shows the biggest jump from worst to best method on AIME24?
questions.expected: Compare the range of bar heights in panel (d) 3B models vs panel (e) 1.5B models on AIME24. The group with larger spread shows more sensitivity to method choice.
questions.requires: Computing within-panel spreads and comparing across panels

figures.panel_description: Left: Deutschland (Germany), Right: EU. Both show Aluminium, Kupfer, Nickel imports from Russia for 2021/2022/2023

questions.question: Für welchen Rohstoff ist der Rückgang von 2021 zu 2023 in Deutschland stärker als in der EU? Belegen Sie dies mit konkreten Zahlen aus beiden Panels.
questions.expected: Nickel DE: 25.1→11.4 (drop 13.7pp). Nickel EU: 24.3→14.6 (drop 9.7pp). Germany's Nickel drop is larger. Also Aluminium DE: 3.6→1.0 (2.6pp) vs EU: 3.2→1.7 (1.5pp).
questions.requires: Reading 4 values (2 panels × 2 years) per metal, computing drops, comparing across panels

questions.question: In welchem Jahr (2021, 2022 oder 2023) sind die Importanteile Deutschlands und der EU am ähnlichsten? Bei welchem Rohstoff?
questions.expected: Compare DE vs EU values for each metal×year combination. Aluminium 2021: DE 3.6 vs EU 3.2 (diff 0.4) is very close.
questions.requires: Systematic comparison of 9 pairs across both panels to find minimum difference

questions.question: Hat Deutschland seine Abhängigkeit von russischem Nickel schneller reduziert als die EU insgesamt? Berechnen Sie die prozentuale Reduktion für beide.
questions.expected: DE Nickel: (25.1-11.4)/25.1 = 54.6% reduction. EU Nickel: (24.3-14.6)/24.3 = 39.9% reduction. Yes, Germany reduced faster.
questions.requires: Computing percentage reduction from both panels and comparing

figures.panel_description: Left: BLEU vs α (knowledge distillation weight), Right: BLEU vs p (mask probability). Both on MuST-C EN-DE.

questions.question: 两个子图的最优参数值分别是多少？对应的BLEU值相同吗？
questions.expected: 左图最优α=0.5,BLEU≈28.53。右图最优p=0.15,BLEU≈28.53。两个最优BLEU值几乎相同。
questions.requires: Finding peak in both panels and comparing peak values

questions.question: 哪个超参数对性能更敏感——α还是p？用两个图的值域范围来支持你的回答。
questions.expected: α的BLEU范围：约28.0到28.53（差0.53）。p的BLEU范围：约28.31到28.53（差0.22）。α更敏感，因为BLEU变化幅度更大。
questions.requires: Computing value ranges from both panels and comparing sensitivity

questions.question: 如果你必须固定一个参数为次优值，固定α=0.1和固定p=0.45哪个带来更大的性能损失？
questions.requires: Reading specific values from both panels and comparing performance penalties

figures.panel_description: Left: Bruttoanlageinvestitionen (% des BIP), Right: Nettoanlageinvestitionen (% des BIP). Both 1991-2023 with Bund/Länder/Gemeinden stacked bars.

questions.question: In welchem Zeitraum divergieren Brutto- und Nettoinvestitionen am stärksten? Was bedeutet eine große Differenz zwischen beiden?
questions.expected: When gross is high but net is low or negative, it means investments barely cover depreciation. Need to compare trends across both panels to find when they diverge most.
questions.requires: Comparing trend shapes across both panels and interpreting the economic meaning

questions.question: Die Nettoinvestitionen (rechtes Panel) werden in manchen Jahren negativ. Ist der Bund, die Länder oder die Gemeinden hauptsächlich für die negativen Werte verantwortlich?
questions.expected: Need to identify which colored segment (Bund/Länder/Gemeinden) goes below zero in the right panel's stacked bars.
questions.requires: Reading component-level detail from one panel while understanding structure from the other

questions.question: Hat die Bahnreform (markiert in beiden Panels) einen sichtbaren Effekt auf die Investitionsmuster? Vergleichen Sie die Trends vor und nach der Reform in beiden Panels.
questions.expected: Need to find the Bahnreform marker in both panels and compare pre/post trends for both gross and net investments.
questions.requires: Locating an annotation in both panels and comparing surrounding trends
